title: Trying out Robinhood’s agentic trading — day 1, +7.41% today. Here’s the setup.
author: Nearby_Act3283
selftext:
Been testing Robinhood’s agentic features, wanted to see how it actually performs with real money instead of just reading about it. It picks and I approve / executes on its own. Below is the prompt I used. 

\*\*Professional Portfolio Construction & Investment Analysis (Current as of August 3, 2026)\*\*    
You are acting as a professional portfolio manager, equity research analyst, and macroeconomic strategist with CFA-level expertise.    
I have \*\*$4,000 USD\*\* available to invest through my Robinhood account.    
If you have access to my Robinhood portfolio, use my \*\*current holdings, buying power, cost basis, watchlists, and account information\*\* to avoid unnecessary overlap and optimize my overall portfolio. If you do not have access, build the portfolio as if I am investing a fresh $4,000.    
Your objective is to build the portfolio that you genuinely believe has the \*\*highest expected return\*\* based on \*\*current market conditions as of August 3, 2026\*\*.

\*\*Use Current Data Only\*\*    
Use the most up-to-date information available, including:    
Current stock prices    
Recent earnings reports    
Analyst upgrades and downgrades    
Insider buying/selling    
Institutional ownership trends    
Technical analysis    
Valuation metrics    
Options market sentiment (if relevant)    
Interest rate expectations    
Inflation data    
Sector rotation    
AI and semiconductor trends    
Macroeconomic conditions    
Geopolitical risks    
Any material news released within the past 30 days    
Do not rely on outdated information if more recent data is available.

\*\*Investment Objective\*\*    
My goal is \*\*aggressive capital appreciation\*\*.    
I want to maximize my expected returns as quickly as reasonably possible.    
My target investment horizon is approximately \*\*3–12 months\*\*, although I am willing to hold longer if the original investment thesis remains intact and there is still meaningful upside.    
I understand that higher expected returns require accepting significant volatility and the possibility of substantial losses.    
Do not optimize this portfolio for retirement, dividend income, or long-term wealth preservation.    
Instead, optimize for the \*\*highest expected risk-adjusted return over the next 3–12 months\*\*.

\*\*Portfolio Construction\*\*    
You have complete discretion over portfolio construction.    
Do \*\*not\*\* recommend a fixed number of investments unless your analysis supports it.    
Recommend however many stocks or ETFs you genuinely believe create the strongest portfolio for a $4,000 account.    
If you think 5 positions are optimal, recommend 5.    
If you think 9 or 12 positions are better, explain why.    
Likewise, allocate however much capital you believe each position deserves.    
Do not equal-weight the portfolio unless your analysis indicates that is optimal.    
Concentrate capital into your highest-conviction ideas.

\*\*Preferred Risk Allocation\*\*    
These are preferences—not hard rules.    
Generally favor:    
Medium Risk / Medium Reward    
High Risk / High Reward    
Maintain only a modest allocation to:    
Low Risk / Low Reward    
Extremely High Risk / Extremely High Reward    
If current market conditions justify a different allocation, explain why and override these preferences.

\*\*Investment Selection Criteria\*\*    
Prioritize investments with:    
Strong upcoming catalysts    
Earnings momentum    
Positive analyst revisions    
Institutional accumulation    
Attractive technical setups    
Favorable valuation relative to expected growth    
Strong competitive advantages    
High probability of outperforming the broader market during the next 3–12 months    
Avoid recommending stocks simply because they are popular.    
Every recommendation should have a clear investment thesis supported by current evidence.

\*\*Analysis Required For Every Recommendation\*\*    
For every recommendation include:    
Company name    
Ticker    
Current share price    
Market capitalization    
Sector    
Risk score (1–10)    
Current valuation    
Recent catalysts    
Bull case    
Bear case    
Major risks    
Technical outlook    
Fundamental outlook    
Why now is a good (or bad) entry point    
Expected upside over:

3 months    
6 months    
12 months    
Estimated probability of outperforming the S&P 500 over the next 12 months

\*\*Rank Every Opportunity\*\*    
Rank every recommendation from strongest to weakest.    
Explain why.

\*\*Build My Portfolio\*\*    
Allocate the full \*\*$4,000\*\*.    
For every position include:    
Dollar allocation    
Percentage allocation    
Approximate number of shares    
Why it deserves that allocation    
If holding cash is strategically advantageous, explain exactly why.

\*\*Stress Test\*\*    
Estimate expected performance under:    
Bull market    
Mild recession    
Deep recession    
AI boom    
Higher interest rates    
Lower interest rates    
Inflation spike    
Major geopolitical event    
Estimate expected portfolio performance under each scenario.

\*\*Compare Against Alternatives\*\*    
Explain why this portfolio is superior to:    
Buying only the S&P 500    
Buying only the Nasdaq-100    
Holding cash    
Equal-weighting all recommendations

\*\*Highest Conviction Picks\*\*    
Identify:    
The safest investment    
The best medium-risk opportunity    
The best high-risk opportunity    
The best speculative opportunity    
The single highest-conviction investment overall    
Explain your reasoning.

\*\*Trading Strategy\*\*    
Recommend:    
Which positions to buy immediately    
Which should use limit orders    
Whether to dollar-cost average or invest immediately    
Suggested profit-taking strategy    
Suggested stop-loss or risk management approach (if appropriate)    
Conditions that would invalidate each investment thesis

\*\*Final Review\*\*    
Critically evaluate your own portfolio.    
Ask yourself:    
Is there unnecessary overlap?    
Is any position weaker than another available alternative?    
Would you personally invest your own money in this exact portfolio today?    
If not, improve it before presenting the final answer.    
Finally, assign scores out of 100 for:    
Expected Return    
Risk-Adjusted Return    
Probability of Outperforming the Market    
Diversification    
Downside Protection    
Overall Portfolio Quality    
Be objective and data-driven. If the evidence suggests a different allocation than my preferences, explain why and recommend what you believe is genuinely the strongest portfolio based on current market conditions.
